title: Quarterly Reliability Surge: Charter + Staffing Notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact working charter for a focused, quarter-long "Reliability Surge" to accelerate SLO adoption across product teams. The Surge combines staffing fast-ships (embedded SRE/Platform pairings), rapid experiments that prove cost/latency tradeoffs, and a lightweight measurement + rollout pattern so feature teams can opt-in and graduate to steady-state guardrails.

High-level goals (success criteria):
- 6 customer-facing services have production SLOs (latency/availability) instrumented and validated in the quarter.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO breaches reduced by 40% for participating services.
- Two operational runbooks per service (oncall + degradation fallback) created and exercised.
- At least one cross-service optimization (e.g., prefix cache share or batching policy) reduces per-token cost 10% for targeted workload.

Scope (in/out):
In-scope: user-facing model serving paths (generation API, chat routes, embeddings), routing logic that affects latency, telemetry pipelines for request/response/time-to-first-byte.
Out-of-scope: infra provisioning (GPU procurement), long-term platform re-architecture, enterprise private-deploy sales negotiations.

Phases and cadence:
- Week 0 (kickoff): stakeholder intake, initial risk scan, assign pairings.
- Weeks 1-4 (Discovery + instrumentation sprint): quick SLO definition workshop with feature teams; implement metrics, add alerts; baseline telemetry.
- Weeks 5-8 (Pilot experiments): run 2x micro-experiments per service (e.g., KV cache TTL change, batching window tweak); gather signal.
- Weeks 9-11 (Harden + Runbooks): capture playbooks, oncall handover practice, run a simulated degradation tabletop.
- Week 12 (Handoff + Retrospective): finalize SLO contracts, document lessons, decide which services graduate to steady maintenance.

Staffing & responsibilities (working RACI style):
- Surge Lead (Aisha Patel): overall program owner, cross-team escalations, sponsor syncs.
- Embedded SRE (assigned per service): responsible for alerting, runbooks, test execution, TTL experiments (R).
- Platform Engineer (pairing): implements observability plumbing, batching/caching configuration, release automation (A/C).
- Product Engineer (service owner): defines user impact thresholds, helps design rollback policies (C).
- Data/Observability SME: builds dashboards and helps set SLI thresholds (C).
- Customer Success (as-needed): communicates potential user impact during experiments (I).

Notes on allocation:
- Embedded SREs will be 0.4 FTE for Discovery/Pilot, 0.2 FTE for Harden/Handoff. Plan for 3 full-time temporary contractors if multiple services require deep investigation.

Experiment matrix (example rows):
- Experiment A: KV cache prefix sharing across chat variants. Metric: p95 latency, cache hit rate, token cost delta. Hypothesis: shared prefixes increase cache hit and reduce p95 by 12% with <2% error inflation.
- Experiment B: Aggressive batching for low-latency tails. Metric: time-to-first-byte, batch size distribution, request timeout rate. Hypothesis: batch window + adaptive batching reduces cost 8% without increasing p95 beyond SLO.
- Experiment C: Model fallback chain (quantized fallback during overload). Metric: user-visible error rate, latency, quality regression score. Hypothesis: controlled fallback reduces error budget burn during capacity spikes.

Measurement and telemetry plan:
- Canonical SLOs: availability (success rate of 2xx tokens per request) and latency (p95 time-to-first-token for generation endpoints).
- SLIs captured: request success, TTFB, tail latencies, error budget burn rate, deployment triggers.
- Dashboards: per-service SLO dashboard (tokenized throughput, error budget projection, experiment overlays).
- Alerting: two-tier alerts: minor (early-warning when burn > 10% of weekly budget) and major (immediate paging for >25% burn sustained 10m).

Risk register (top risks + mitigations):
- Risk: Experiments cause customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: Canary traffic gates, dark-launch experiments, CS pre-notify.
- Risk: Insufficient FTE to finish instrumentation. Mitigation: prioritize 6 services; shift nonparticipating teams to phase 2.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps (missing traces, skewed p95). Mitigation: short instrumentation spike to validate sampling; fall back to tracer-based p95 approximations.

Communication & decision rhythm:
- Weekly Surge sync (30m) — operational checkpoints, blocked items, owner wins.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder demo (45m) — show dashboards, experiment outcomes, escalate tradeoffs.
- Ad-hoc war room for major SLO breach (90m) — SREs + Eng leads + CS.
- Asynchronous updates in #reliability-surge Slack channel with a pinned MITIGATION log.

Onboarding checklist for a participating service:
- SLO definition signed off by product + SRE.
- Metrics pipeline: request id, latency, success tag, token counts instrumented.
- Baseline dashboard created with weekly trend 180d (if available).
- Runbook skeleton (3-step incident & rollback) committed to repo.
- Experiment plan doc linked and JIRA ticket created.

Templates included (links):
- SLO definition template (short): objective, SLI, measurement window, error budget, owner.
- Experiment report template: hypothesis, setup, metrics, outcome, follow-up.

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Threshold for graduation: what absolute error budget velocity qualifies a service to graduate vs remain in Surge? Proposal: average weekly burn <5% for 4 consecutive weeks.
- Contractor hiring: approve 3x 12-week contractors for January–March? Need budget sign-off.
- Platform changes that require infra freeze window — recommend a 2-day freeze for critical changes during Week 9–10.

Next immediate steps (this doc as action list):
1) Finalize pairings: Aisha to confirm Embedded SRE list by 2026-01-20.
2) Run intake survey to collect service owners and current telemetry gaps (deadline 2026-01-22).
3) Create JIRA epic and add initial experiment backlog (owner: Jonah).
4) Book weekly Surge sync in calendars and create Slack channel.

Notes to self / informal reminders:
- Keep templates tiny and explicit — feature teams ignore long docs.
- Use experimental bandit approach: prefer smaller multi-service wins vs one giant refactor.
- Capture one clear customer story per service to make SLOs concrete in demos.

If you are reading and want to join the Surge: ping me (Aisha) with service name, tech lead, and current telemetry gaps.
summary: Working charter for a quarter-long Reliability Surge: staffing, experiments, measurement, and handoff checklist to accelerate SLO adoptions across 6 services. Draft status; next steps include pairing confirmation, intake survey, and initial JIRA epic creation.
